claims.statement: A task row has one of five statuses: proposed, seeded, worked, verified, packaged.
The task transition trigger permits verified to packaged, or verified to seeded with a pending requirements revision; it has no Scribe transition.
Agent proposals start proposed, and operator tasks can start seeded.
Task dispatch maps Worked to Verifier and Verified directly to Packager.
Dispatch starts the Strategist when no task can proceed, no proposal decision awaits an answer, and the role is available.
A Verifier pass requires --sha, a correction forbids --sha, and --correction is legal only with outcome correct; every verdict requires --evidence.
The Verifier allowance counts rejected corrections after the initial rejection and resets on a pass; merge repairs return the task to Seeded for each conflict.
The Worker status moves to worked when the captured submission is recorded, not in the mc complete terminal itself.
mc packet decide accepts exactly one of approve, revise, or cancel; approve forbids a reason and revise and cancel require one.
requireDurableRunArtifact refuses a recorded path outside the artifact root, outside the run's own planes, missing, non-regular, empty, or over its size bound.
snapshotRunArtifact stores the submitted bytes as a read-only snapshot-<sha256> file beside the source.
requirements_version can rise only by one, only to the text of a pending revision, and only on an undecided, unarchived row.
The shared environment skill requires fresh assigned source for Worker, Verifier, Packager, and Scribe runs while retaining the Project home.
A requirements revision resolves an operator decision report, preserves the task base and retained work, and returns the task to Seeded.
Proposal criteria must name checks that the Worker and Verifier can run in an agent container, and the Arbiter must require container-checkable criteria.
The proposal directives exclude criteria that require host access, a Docker daemon, macOS interfaces, additional container privileges, or hosted continuous integration.
Strategist and Arbiter briefs include up to 10 cancelled tasks and rejected tasks within a total limit of 20.
The Strategist directive forbids equivalent historical work; the Arbiter directive points to the command skill for history comparison.
The skill permits active or historical duplicate references; the command exception check requires active work beyond Proposed or archived approved work outside the pool.
The input tests check Arbiter history instructions and Strategist duplicate rules; dispatch tests check historical entries and Project isolation.

The Packager directive permits Project instructions to replace the default packet section structure and omit the glossary while retaining all decision evidence, material behavior, risks, and verification results.
The Packager directive requires a self-contained packet.html, embedded media, no scripts, and preservation of the dashboard page style.
The shared environment skill assigns provider credential retention and access renewal to the host.
ArbiterDecide accepts only invalid_criteria as a rejection category and forbids combining it with duplicate_of.
An ordinary all-reject batch with no other ready task requires every rejection to cite a valid duplicate or declare invalid criteria.
ArbiterDecide applies the batch, ends the run, and releases the lease in one transaction.
The Verifier submits CORRECT when a task causes a regression outside acceptance criteria or a new or changed test fails.
The Review Packet preserves unchanged failures, base comparisons, and UNVERIFIED entries separately from the task verdict.
The Worker instruction audit records retained rules, shorter instructions, and unchanged command forms and runtime authority for task 56.
The Worker instruction audit records an unchanged operator-home failure and unavailable host checks in its historical merge repair validation.
Worker and Verifier procedures select outcomes for unavailable criterion checks and new or changed tests by cause, while preserving independent work and unverified evidence.
The Strategist and its subagents can use internet research; further research needs a fact that can change task selection.
StrategistPropose checks role, run identity, a subjectless lease, Project scope, and the two-task limit before it commits proposals and ends the run.
The Strategist command skill permits an empty proposal batch and defines terminals for execution problems, required operator decisions, and customization conflicts.
The Strategist traces useful results, checks existing capabilities, and weighs the full cost before it selects candidates.
The Strategist directive requires two proposals, each with evidence, a useful result, current value, substantial effort or risk, and scoped container checks.
The Arbiter contract includes the promotion limit and criteria rules, and the directive requires one promotion unless all-reject rules apply.
The Arbiter directive requires description-based overlap checks and protects active and merged work while permitting extensions of merged work.
The Arbiter skill requires a duplicate reference or invalid_criteria category for each rejection in an all-reject batch.
The verdict command rejects unknown fields and trailing data, then applies only a batch that covers the exact snapshotted pool.
The Arbiter ranks proposals by contribution to the Vision relative to cost, considering results, feasible benefits, and new capabilities.
The command counts other ready Project tasks before requiring all-reject exceptions; a pending pool requirements revision bypasses that guard.
